textos.Un pueblo de marisma en la costa, al sur: A marsh town on the coast, southeast of Puerto Bravo: rice fields, a lagoon full of birds, eel fishermen and some closed salt flats that someone uses at night. Four missions against smugglers in the channels, with a decision at the end, an honest job, a duck blind shotgun, an eel fisherman's spear, a marsh skiff, the cooperative's station wagon, a race through the rice fields, fishing in the lagoon, treasure hunting and a character.
textos.La carretera de la costa, que baja entre: The coast road, running down through pines and rice fields to Marisma Negra.
textos.Bocana de los Caños de Marisma Negra, de: Los Caños Mouth, Marisma Negra, from the sea
textos.La entrada del caño grande de Marisma Ne: The mouth of Marisma Negra's main channel, on the coast, between Puerto Bravo and Cala Brava.
textos.En la Taberna El Anguilero, un viejo ang: At El Anguilero Tavern, an old eel fisherman says someone is cutting his nets at night.
textos.Cuarenta años poniendo nasas en los caño: Forty years setting traps in the channels and nobody ever touched them. This week they've cut them three times.
textos.¿Y quién va a querer unas nasas de angui: And who would want a bunch of eel traps?
textos.Nadie. Las cortan porque estorban. De no: Nobody. They cut them because they're in the way. At night a boat comes through with the engine off, rowing, and my nets block its path.
textos.Tú no eres de aquí, foraster[o|a], y eso: You're not from here, outsider, and that suits me: nobody knows you. Go up to the Old Lock, by the rice fields, and see what's there.
textos.Ve a la Compuerta de la Esclusa Vieja, a: Go to the Old Lock Floodgate, northeast of town, among the rice fields.
textos.Recoge la nasa que se ha quedado enganch: Pick up the trap that got caught on the floodgate.
textos.una nasa cortada con un precinto de plás: a cut trap with a plastic seal
textos.La nasa está cortada a cuchillo. Del aro: The trap was cut with a knife. A blue plastic seal hangs from the hoop, the kind they put on sacks.
textos.Sacos precintados en una marisma donde s: Sealed sacks in a marsh where there's nothing but rice and eels. Something else is moving through here.
textos.Vuelve a la Taberna El Anguilero y enséñ: Go back to El Anguilero Tavern and show Amador what you found.
textos.Ese azul lo conozco. Era el de las Salin: I know that blue. It belonged to the San Ginés Salt Flats, before they shut them down. They've been dead for ten years.
textos.Muertas de día, Amador. De noche hay luz: Dead by day, Amador. At night there's a light on in the warehouse. Half the town knows it and nobody says a thing.
textos.Pues habla con Celia, la guarda de la la: Then talk to Celia, the lagoon warden. She spends all day in the bird observatory and sees more than anyone.
textos.Celia, la guarda de la laguna, ve entrar: Celia, the lagoon warden, sees a boat with no lights come in through the main channel every other night.
textos.Así que tú eres [el|la] que anda pregunt: So you're the one asking around about the salt flats. Amador says your name is Dani.
textos.Y tú eres la que lo ve todo desde aquí a: And you're the one who sees everything from up here.
textos.Veo garzas, flamencos y, desde hace un m: I see herons, flamingos and, for the past month, a boat with no lights coming in through the main channel every other night.
textos.He dado tres partes a la Guardia Civil y: I've filed three reports with the Guardia Civil and nobody has come. Get close to the salt flats and watch the warehouse. Don't let them see you.
textos.Vigila las Salinas de San Ginés sin que: Watch the San Ginés Salt Flats without being seen. When you hear footsteps, stay still or crouch with X.
textos.Tres hombres sacan sacos precintados del: Three men carry sealed sacks out of the salt flats warehouse and take them down the channel to a boat with no lights. One of them, in a cap, gives the orders.
textos.Sigue al hombre de la gorra sin que te d: Follow the man in the cap without being spotted. Go by his footsteps.
textos.El hombre de la gorra entra en la lonja: The man in the cap goes into the fish market through the back door and greets the manager like an old friend.
textos.Dos noches más y vaciamos el almacén. Y: Two more nights and we empty the warehouse. And nobody touches that old man's traps again, or he'll start talking.
textos.Vuelve al Observatorio de aves y cuéntal: Go back to the Bird Observatory and tell Celia what you heard.
textos.Salvador Ruano. Fue capataz de las salin: Salvador Ruano. He was foreman at the salt flats until they closed, and it seems he kept the keys.
He called Amador old. They know each other.
textos.Desde críos. No sé qué guarda en esos sa: Since they were kids. I don't know what he keeps in those sacks, but it isn't salt. Go see Amador: he'll know how to get at him.
textos.Los hombres de Ruano duermen en el almac: Ruano's men sleep in the salt flats warehouse, next to the cargo.
textos.Salvador Ruano... Fuimos juntos a la esc: Salvador Ruano... We went to school together. Even back then he sold what wasn't his.
textos.Dice que en dos noches vacían el almacén: He says they'll empty the warehouse in two nights. If we wait, they'll be gone with everything.
textos.Entonces no esperes. Esta noche duermen: Then don't wait. Tonight four of his people are sleeping there, outsiders who don't even know where they're stepping.
textos.Llévate mi escopeta de puesto y la fisga: Take my duck blind shotgun and the spear. The shotgun for distance; the spear if they get on top of you.
textos.Y vuelve enter[o|a], Dani, que la cuenta: And come back in one piece, Dani, because nobody's going to let you off your tab at the tavern.
textos.Ve a las Salinas de San Ginés y acaba co: Go to the San Ginés Salt Flats and take out Ruano's men.
textos.Recoge el cuaderno de mareas que hay sob: Pick up the tide notebook on the warehouse table.
textos.Los tiros se han oído hasta en el pueblo: The shots were heard all the way in town. Shake off the Guardia Civil patrol.
textos.Los sacos no llevan sal: llevan cartones: The sacks don't hold salt: they hold cartons of cigarettes and unbranded watches, wrapped in plastic to keep the water out.
textos.El cuaderno apunta cada marea alta del m: The notebook lists every high tide of the month and, next to each one, a van's license plate and a single word: city.
textos.Lo sacan por los caños con la marea y lo: They take it out through the channels with the tide and drive it up to Puerto Bravo by road. Clever, Ruano.
textos.Ruano ha cargado lo que le queda y se va: Ruano has loaded what he has left and is leaving for the city tonight on the coast road.
textos.Marisma Negra: los caños vuelven a ser d: Marisma Negra: the channels belong to the eel fishermen again
textos.Esa noche las anguilas entran por el cañ: That night the eels come in through the main channel with no one blocking their way. At the tavern they toast Amador's boat, which is now yours, and Celia goes back to counting herons.
textos.Ruano sabe que fuiste tú. Ha cargado lo: Ruano knows it was you. He's loaded what he had left into the fish market's refrigerated van and he's leaving for the city tonight.
textos.He vuelto a llamar a la Guardia Civil. L: I've called the police again. They'll be here in an hour, and by then Ruano will already be in Puerto Bravo.
textos.Pues no llega. ¿Por dónde sale?: Then he won't get there. Which way does he go out?
textos.Por la carretera de la costa, que es la: By the coast road, it's the only one. Stop him before he leaves town, Dani. Take more shells.
textos.Alcanza y destroza la furgoneta frigoríf: Catch and wreck Ruano's refrigerated van within five minutes.
textos.Recoge la llave del almacén, que ha salt: Pick up the warehouse key that flew out of the van.
textos.Esto no es mío, foraster[o|a]. Yo solo l: This isn't mine, outsider. I just keep it. The ones who pay are in the city, and they're not going to like this.
Then let them come looking for it in the marsh. We know the way now.
textos.Ruano se aleja cojeando hacia los pinos: Ruano limps off toward the pines and doesn't look back.
textos.Tienes el cuaderno de mareas de Ruano, c: You have Ruano's tide notebook, with dates and license plates. A dark car pulls over on the shoulder and a well-dressed man offers you money for it. What do you do?
textos.Dárselo a Celia para la Guardia Civil: Give it to Celia for the Guardia Civil
textos.Lo justo. Ganas fama en Marisma Negra y: The right thing. You gain street reputation in Marisma Negra and earn nothing.
textos.Le dices al hombre del coche que el cuad: You tell the man in the car that the notebook already has an owner. He leaves without saying goodbye.
textos.Vendérselo al hombre del coche por 900 e: Sell it to the man in the car for 900 euros
textos.Cobras bien, y los que pagaban a Ruano s: You get paid well, and the people who paid Ruano will keep using the channels.
textos.El hombre cuenta los billetes sobre el c: The man counts the bills on the hood without taking off his gloves.
textos.Ve al Embarcadero de los Caños, donde te: Go to Los Caños Pier, where Amador and Celia are waiting for you.
textos.Con este cuaderno no hay quien mire para: With this notebook nobody can look the other way. Tomorrow the lagoon will be full of uniforms, and for once I'm glad.
textos.¿Y el cuaderno? No, no me lo digas. Al m: And the notebook? No, don't tell me. At least Ruano won't be coming back here.
textos.Esta noche las anguilas entran por el ca: Tonight the eels come in through the main channel with no one blocking their way.
textos.La barca de mi padre es tuya, Dani. Cala: My father's boat is yours, Dani. It draws very little water and goes where nobody else can. It's tied up right here.
textos.Y en la taberna tienes plato de arroz pa: And at the tavern you've got a plate of rice all winter long. Welcome to Marisma Negra.
textos.Trabajo honrado: el Comedor de la Cofrad: Honest work: the Guild Soup Kitchen has run out of rice and fish.
textos.Los jueves cierro la taberna y echo una: On Thursdays I close the tavern and lend a hand at the Guild soup kitchen. Today we have no rice and no fish.
textos.La cooperativa nos regala diez sacos. Co: The cooperative is giving us ten sacks. Take their station wagon, it's unlocked, and bring it here without spilling anything.
textos.Eso después, en la lonja. Pregunta por l: That comes later, at the fish market. Ask for the soup kitchen's crate, they already know.
textos.Recoge la ranchera junto a la Cooperativ: Pick up the station wagon next to La Espiga Rice Cooperative. It's unlocked.
textos.Lleva la ranchera con los sacos al Comed: Take the station wagon with the sacks to the Guild Soup Kitchen in four minutes without bumping it.
textos.Recoge en la Lonja de la Anguila la caja: Pick up the soup kitchen's crate of fish at the Eel Fish Market.
textos.la caja de pescado del comedor: the soup kitchen's crate of fish
textos.Vuelve al Comedor de la Cofradía antes d: Get back to the Guild Soup Kitchen before they open the doors. You have two and a half minutes.
textos.Justo a tiempo. Hoy comen treinta person: Just in time. Thirty people get to eat today thanks to you.
textos.Guárdame un plato, que huele que aliment: Save me a plate, the smell alone could feed you.
textos.La escopeta de los cazadores de patos de: The shotgun of the marsh duck hunters: long, heavy and with a shot you can hear all across the lagoon.
textos.Un tridente corto de hierro con mango de: A short iron trident with a cane handle. It's for spearing eels in the mud, and for keeping someone at a distance.
textos.Una barca de fondo plano con un fuera bo: A flat-bottomed boat with an outboard motor that barely makes a sound. It draws so little water it gets through the narrowest channels. Press the J key to run courier jobs between piers.
textos.Una ranchera con la caja llena de sacos: A station wagon with the back full of rice sacks and mud up to the mirrors. Press the J key to do the deliveries.
textos.Los Caños: canales de agua salobre entre: Los Caños: brackish water channels among the reeds, flat-bottomed boats beached in the mud and, in the distance, the San Ginés Salt Flats, closed ten years ago. At night all you hear are the frogs and, now and then, an oar.
textos.Marisma Negra, un pueblo de casas bajas: Marisma Negra, a town of low whitewashed houses with a black tar base to keep the damp from rising. It smells of toasted rice, mud and smoked eel.
textos.Los Arrozales: tablas de agua quieta has: Los Arrozales: paddies of still water as far as the eye can see, irrigation ditches, herons and the rice cooperative. At the far end, the Old Lock floodgate separates the fresh water from the salt water.
textos.La carretera de la costa, que sube entre: The coast road, climbing through pines and rice fields up to Puerto Bravo.
textos.Una marquesina de chapa con un banco y u: A sheet-metal shelter with a bench and a timetable nobody keeps.
textos.Un andén corto entre eucaliptos y una ta: A short platform among eucalyptus trees and a ticket window open two hours a day. Trains leave from here for the other towns you can reach by land.
textos.Anguila ahumada colgada sobre la barra,: Smoked eel hanging over the bar, dice, jug wine and a board with jobs. Toñi runs it and Amador sits here.
textos.De todo un poco, botas de agua de todas: A bit of everything, rubber boots in every size and a gas pump at the door.
textos.Una ventanilla, un cajero y un calendari: One teller window, an ATM and a cooperative calendar from three years ago.
textos.Una plaza de tierra con cuatro moreras y: A dirt square with four mulberry trees and a freshwater fountain, the only one in town that doesn't taste of salt.
textos.Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de los Caños: Nuestra Señora de los Caños Church
textos.Una iglesia blanca con una cigüeña en la: A white church with a stork on the bell gable. Inside hang votive offerings from boats that came back from a flood.
textos.Una casa baja con patio de parra, ahumad: A low house with a vine-covered patio, a smokehouse in the yard and a garage for two vehicles.
textos.El consultorio del pueblo. La médica vie: The town clinic. The doctor comes three days a week and the rest of the time it's the nurse, who knows more than many doctors.
textos.Escopetas de puesto para los patos, fisg: Blind shotguns for duck hunting, eel spears, shells and hand-carved wooden decoys.
textos.Repelente de mosquitos en todas sus form: Mosquito repellent in every form, band-aids and first aid kits.
textos.Arreglan motores fuera borda, tractores: They fix outboard motors, tractors and whatever you bring them, even if it's covered in mud.
textos.La Cofradía de anguileros da de comer a: The eel fishermen's guild feeds anyone who needs it. Toñi cooks on Thursdays. There are never enough hands.
textos.Seis habitaciones con mosquitera y desay: Six rooms with mosquito nets and a breakfast of toast with olive oil.
textos.La cooperativa del arroz, en venta desde: The rice cooperative, for sale since the whole board retired. Earns money every midnight. Its station wagon is always at the door: get in and press J to do the deliveries.
textos.Jornadas en los arrozales, en la siega y: Day jobs in the rice fields, at the harvest and at the floodgates.
textos.Arroz de marisma en paella de leña y ang: Marsh rice in a wood-fired paella pan and eel from the lagoon. Long tables and even longer chats after the meal.
textos.En fiestas se corre por los caminos de l: During the town festival they race along the ditch roads. The winner is whoever doesn't end up in a rice paddy.
textos.Una tabla de arroz enorme, con garzas qu: A huge rice paddy, with herons as still as statues and the murmur of water along the ditch.
textos.Una era de cemento donde se seca el arro: A concrete threshing floor where rice is dried in September. The rest of the year the kids play here.
textos.Una compuerta de hierro oxidado que sepa: A rusty iron floodgate that separates the rice fields from the main channel. When the tide rises, the salt water pushes and the gate creaks.
textos.Una pista de tierra apisonada entre arro: A packed-dirt strip among the rice fields, used mostly by crop-dusting planes. Scheduled light planes come and go, and light planes are for rent.
textos.Un muelle de tablones sobre pilotes. Por: A plank dock on pilings. The main channel leads out to the open sea.
textos.Venden y reparan barcas. Las dejan amarr: They sell and repair boats. They're left moored at the pier.
Eels are auctioned here at dawn. They buy everything you take out of the lagoon or the sea.
textos.Una lengua de arena entre el mar y la ma: A tongue of sand between the sea and the marsh. The floods leave all sorts of things here.
textos.Agua oscura y quieta, y debajo, anguilas: Dark, still water, and beneath it, eels and mullet.
textos.Una caseta de madera sobre pilotes con m: A wooden hut on pilings with viewing slits facing the lagoon. Celia, the warden, spends her days here.
textos.Unas salinas cerradas hace diez años: ba: Salt flats closed ten years ago: dry pans, heaps of gray salt and a warehouse with a corrugated asbestos roof. They say it's empty.
textos.Hija y nieta de anguileros de Marisma Ne: Daughter and granddaughter of Marisma Negra eel fishermen. Starts with fishing at level four, some endurance, an eel spear, one hundred sixty euros and a good standing with the neighbors.
